items.body:
## Why

Very large user inputs can push a normal turn start beyond the model context window before Codex has a chance to compact. When that input is recorded first and only rejected later, the oversized content can become durable thread history and make future continuation harder to recover.

## What changed

This PR adds a pre-persistence sizing pass for normal turn starts.

### Turn-start decision flow

For the incoming user message available at the start of `run_turn`:

1. Estimate the model-visible token cost of that incoming user message.
   - Unsupported images are normalized the same way prompt construction does before estimating.
2. If the incoming user message alone exceeds the model context window, reject it immediately before compaction or persistence.
3. Otherwise, compute projected turn size and decide whether to compact before recording the user message.
   - Pre-turn compaction runs when the thread is already at the hard context-window limit.
   - Pre-turn compaction also runs when there is existing history to compact and the projected incoming turn crosses either:
     - the configured auto-compaction threshold for the active scope, or
     - the full model context window in `BodyAfterPrefix` mode.
   - Empty-history first prompts do not trigger a wasted compaction attempt just because the incoming prompt is large.
4. After any pre-turn compaction attempt, re-check whether normalized history + base instructions + incoming user message still exceeds the model context window.
   - If it still does, reject before persisting the user message.
   - If it fits, continue through the existing turn flow and persist/sample normally.

### Scope

* This PR is intentionally scoped to normal turn starts.
* Queued or steered input remains unchanged and can be handled separately.
* The preflight estimate intentionally covers only:
  - prompt-normalized existing history,
  - session base instructions, and
  - the incoming user message already available at turn start.
* It does not attempt to predict later request growth from context diffs, hook-added context, skill/plugin injections, or other downstream request shaping.

## Verification

* `just fmt`
* `cargo test -p codex-core --test all pre_turn_auto_compact`
* `cargo test -p codex-core --test all oversized_incoming_user_input_is_rejected_before_persistence`
* `cargo test -p codex-app-server --test all turn_start_oversized_input_emits_input_too_large_error_notification_v2`
* `just fix -p codex-core`
* `git diff --check`

items.body: ## Why Fixes #16605. A malformed image payload can be persisted into model-visible history and then replayed on later turns or after resume. When the Responses API rejects that replay with an `invalid_value` `.image_url` error, the thread can stay poisoned because the same bad payload is reconstructed and sent again. This PR keeps the fix focused on recognizing those API errors and recovering the thread by rolling back the failed turn. Inline image preflight validation in app-server, protocol conversion, or dynamic tool output paths is intentionally left for a follow-up. ## What changed - Map additional Responses API invalid-image 400 shapes to `CodexErr::InvalidImageRequest()`, including `.image_url` `invalid_value` responses and the empty-base64 image message. - Reuse the existing thread rollback reconstruction path for invalid-image failures so the failed turn is removed from in-memory state and persisted replay history. - Emit a `ThreadRolledBack` event plus a user-facing error when automatic rollback succeeds or fails. - Remove the previous placeholder sanitizer path that replaced image content with `Invalid image`; rollback is now the recovery behavior. - Add a regression for the invalid local-image flow that verifies rollback marker persistence, resume behavior, and that the follow-up request does not replay the bad image or placeholder text. ## Local testing Before: After: Quitting and resuming thread: ## Verification - `cargo fmt --all --check --manifest-path codex-rs/Cargo.toml` - `cargo test -p codex-api --lib map_api_error_maps_invalid_image --manifest-path codex-rs/Cargo.toml` - `cargo test -p codex-api --lib map_api_error_maps_empty_base64_image_message_from_400_body --manifest-path codex-rs/Cargo.toml` - `cargo test -p codex-core --lib context_manager::history::tests --manifest-path codex-rs/Cargo.toml` - `cargo test -p codex-core --lib session::tests::thread_rollback --manifest-path codex-rs/Cargo.toml`

# Why

Follow-up to #22782 and stacked on #22882.

`SubagentStart` gives hooks a lifecycle point once a child agent is being created, but the parent-side `spawn_agent` tool call is also an important context-loading and policy seam. Andrei called out that gap during review of #22782: `spawn_agent|Agent` should participate in the existing `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hook flow so hook authors can react before and after a spawn in the same way they already can for other tools.

# What

- Expose both v1 and v2 `spawn_agent` handlers to `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse`.
- Serialize the canonical hook tool name as `spawn_agent` while accepting `Agent` as a matcher alias.
- Support `updated_input` rewrites for spawn requests, so `PreToolUse` hooks can replace the spawn JSON before the handler parses and executes it.
- Surface the final spawn result through `PostToolUse.tool_response`.
- Add focused handler tests for:
  - v1/v2 pre-hook payloads and `Agent` matcher compatibility
  - v1/v2 `updated_input` rewriting
  - v1/v2 post-hook payloads and serialized spawn results

This stays intentionally scoped to `spawn_agent`; the other collaboration tools remain unchanged.

# Validation

- `cargo test -p codex-core hook_payloads_use_agent_alias_and_support_rewrites`
- `cargo test -p codex-core post_tool_use_payload_exposes_spawn_result`

## Summary
- replace the one-shot lazy remote exec-server cache with a lock-protected current client
- when the cached websocket client is already disconnected, create one fresh websocket client/session on the next `get()`
- keep existing disconnect failure behavior for old process sessions and HTTP body streams; do not add session resume or request retry

## Why
The prior PR direction was trying to grow into session restore: resume the old `session_id`, preserve existing process handles, and add reconnect retry policy. That is more machinery than we want for this slice.

For now, the useful minimum is simpler: later fresh remote operations should not be stuck behind a dead cached websocket client, but anything already attached to the dead connection should fail loudly through the existing disconnect path. The server already has detached-session cleanup via its existing TTL, so this PR does not need to add client-side session preservation.

## What Changed
- `LazyRemoteExecServerClient::get()` now keeps the current concrete client in a small mutex-protected cache plus one async connect lock.
- If that cached client is still connected, `get()` returns it.
- If that cached client is a disconnected websocket client, `get()` creates a brand-new websocket client with a brand-new exec-server session and replaces the cache.
- If that cached client is stdio-backed, behavior stays one-shot: the dead client is returned and later work surfaces the existing disconnect error.
- No `resume_session_id`, backoff, request replay, or existing `RemoteExecProcess` rebinding is added here.
- Added focused websocket coverage that proves two concurrent `get()` calls after disconnect share one fresh replacement client/session.

## Validation
- Ran `just fmt`.
- Did not run tests in this pass.
items.title: Reconnect disconnected exec-server websocket clients with fresh sessions

# Why

PreToolUse and PostToolUse coverage for built-in local tools has been opt-in per tool runtime. That makes every new built-in tool, and every existing tool that missed the wiring, another place where hooks can silently stop applying.

The recent reports around missing hook coverage are symptoms of that shape: the core hook machinery works, but local tools only participate if their runtime remembered to provide the hook payload and updatedInput rewrite path.

# What

This makes the default local tool runtime participate in hooks for local, client-executed tool payloads:

- Builds a generic PreToolUse payload from function, tool_search, and custom tool payloads.
- Applies generic updatedInput rewrites back onto those payloads before execution.
- Builds a generic PostToolUse payload from an explicit typed hook response when available, otherwise from the model-visible tool output.
- Keeps the existing specialized adapters for shell, MCP, apply_patch, and write_stdin behavior where they intentionally project compatibility fields or custom output shapes.
- Adds regression coverage showing that tools like update_plan now fire PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks without bespoke runtime wiring.

The important design choice is that specialized runtimes can still override the defaults, but the default is no longer "no hooks." That should turn future local built-in tools into coverage-by-default instead of whackamole.

# Deviations / Roadbumps

- Hosted Responses tools are intentionally still out of scope. We skipped them because they do not run through the same local CoreToolRuntime execution path, and true PreToolUse enforcement would be misleading once the hosted tool has already executed upstream.
- The generic custom-tool updatedInput path only accepts string replacement. Object-shaped or otherwise structured custom tools should still provide an explicit adapter so the rewrite remains type-aware.
- For PostToolUse, the fallback uses the model-visible output only when the typed output does not provide an explicit hook response. That kept the change small while preserving existing special-case output contracts.
- Local formatting needed an escalated rerun because the repo formatter touched uv cache state outside the workspace sandbox. That was an environment issue, not a code/design change.

# Validation

- `just fmt`
- `just fix -p codex-core`
- `cargo test -p codex-core write_stdin_pre_tool_use_payload_uses_generic_input`
- `cargo test -p codex-core pre_tool_use_blocks_plan_tool_before_execution`
- `cargo test -p codex-core post_tool_use_rewrites_plan_tool_output`
- `cargo test -p codex-core default_pre_tool_use_payload_uses_function_arguments`
- `cargo test -p codex-core default_with_updated_hook_input_rewrites_function_arguments`
- `cargo test -p codex-core default_with_updated_hook_input_rewrites_tool_search_arguments`
- `cargo test -p codex-core default_post_tool_use_payload_uses_model_visible_output`

I did not run the full codex-core workspace suite locally because it is broader and slower; the targeted coverage exercises the changed hook paths.

## Summary
This changes spawned MultiAgentV2 thread children so they can register their thread before slow startup work finishes, instead of blocking the parent on required MCP initialization.

The new path is gated behind `features.multi_agent_v2.async_subagent_startup` and is intentionally limited to pathful `ThreadSpawn` children. That keeps delayed startup failures compatible with the existing parent notification and mailbox semantics.

## What changed
- add a session startup state machine and deferred startup handoff for eligible spawned subagents
- register thread-spawn children before background MCP startup, then resume initialization after `ThreadManager` has published the child
- keep mailbox-triggered work queued while startup is still initializing
- reject direct turn-starting requests with explicit errors while startup is initializing or after startup failure
- notify the parent when deferred startup fails and suppress late failure reporting after shutdown
- add config/schema coverage for the new flag
- add targeted tests for pathful gating, queued mailbox behavior, direct input rejection, parent notification, and shutdown suppression

## Root cause
Required MCP startup was part of synchronous session creation, so a spawned child could not become visible to its parent until all required MCP servers had either initialized or failed. That made slow MCP startup block thread registration entirely.

## Impact
With the flag enabled, the parent can observe the spawned child immediately, while the child stays in `PendingInit` until deferred startup reaches a terminal state. If required MCP startup fails, the parent receives the same style of subagent notification without needing the child to have started a turn first.

items.body:
## Why

A single autonomous Codex turn can repeatedly cycle through execution and automatic compaction when compaction succeeds but leaves the active context above the effective auto-compact trigger. Once a turn is in that state, another automatic compaction is usually not progress; it can keep the same turn alive indefinitely.

This PR adds a circuit breaker before dispatching another automatic compaction after 3 consecutive no-progress automatic compactions. A real accepted user steer can reset the limiter, but internal queued work cannot.

## What changed

- Add an internal automatic compaction limiter for regular turns.
- Keep the limiter at `RegularTask::run()` scope so it survives repeated `run_turn()` invocations for the same active turn.
- Track consecutive successful automatic compactions that still leave the turn over the effective compaction trigger across local compaction, remote v1, and remote v2.
- Stop before dispatching the next automatic compaction after 3 no-progress compactions by emitting `CodexErrorInfo::ContextWindowExceeded`, logging limiter state, and treating the turn result as terminal so the regular task loop does not restart with a fresh limiter.
- Reset the limiter after successful progress or accepted `TurnInput::UserInput(_)`; internal `ResponseInputItem` work such as `/goal` continuation, budget steering, mailbox delivery, or injected response items does not reset the counter.
- Mark the active turn terminal on the guard path so late steer/injected input cannot enqueue into the same stopped turn.
- When terminal cleanup finds already-staged pending input, reject pending `UserInput` explicitly and queue pending `ResponseInputItem` work for the next turn instead of silently dropping the whole queue.
- Leave manual `/compact` unaffected.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p codex-core terminal_active_turn_rejects_new_pending_input`
- `cargo test -p codex-core --test all pending_input::steered_user_input_resets_auto_compact_limit`
- `cargo test -p codex-core --test all pending_input::steered_user_input_is_rejected_when_auto_compact_guard_fires`
- `cargo test -p codex-core --test all compact::auto_compact_stops_after_consecutive_no_progress_compactions`

## Why

Project-local `.codex/config.toml` is loaded behind the project trust boundary. If that config is malformed while the project is untrusted or not yet trusted, failing startup is harsher than necessary because Codex would not apply that project-local layer anyway. Instead, we should tell the user what happened and continue with the disabled layer ignored.

Trusted project-local config still fails loudly, because the user explicitly opted into loading it. Required config layers such as user, profile, system, and managed config are unchanged.

## What changed

- Added a startup warning for malformed project-local config when the corresponding project layer is disabled by trust.
- Kept trusted project-local config parse errors as hard failures.
- Applied the same warning-and-ignore behavior to malformed linked-worktree root hook config when the project is disabled.

## Test coverage

Added config-loader regression tests for:

- Explicitly untrusted malformed project config warning and ignored disabled layer.
- Unknown-trust malformed project config warning and ignored disabled layer.
- Trusted malformed project config still returning an `InvalidData` parse error.
- Malformed linked-worktree root hook config warning when the project is disabled.
items.title: Warn on malformed disabled project config

## Why

Remote compaction v2 sends a normal `/responses` request with a compaction trigger. It should follow the retry semantics used by normal Responses streaming calls: retry transient stream/request failures with the provider stream retry budget, and fall back from WebSockets to HTTPS when the websocket retry budget is exhausted.

## What changed

- Add a v2 compaction retry loop that uses `stream_max_retries`, matching normal Responses turn retries.
- Retry retryable request-open and post-open stream collection failures through the same loop.
- Use the existing 200ms exponential backoff and requested retry delay handling used by normal turn retries.
- Emit the same `Reconnecting... n/max` stream-error notification pattern.
- Fall back from WebSockets to HTTPS after the stream retry budget is exhausted, matching normal turn behavior.
- Keep final remote-compaction failure logging after retries/fallback are exhausted.
- Treat compact stream EOF before `response.completed` as a retryable stream failure.
- Add compact v2 regression coverage with `request_max_retries = 0` and `stream_max_retries = 2`, covering both request-open failure and opened-stream EOF in one end-to-end test.

## Tests

- `just fmt`
- `cargo test -p codex-core remote_compact_v2`
- `just fix -p codex-core`

The zsh release workflow currently publishes macOS arm64 and Linux zsh fork artifacts, but no macOS x64 artifact. That leaves `x86_64-apple-darwin` Codex packages without a bundled `codex-resources/zsh/bin/zsh`, so `shell_zsh_fork` cannot be enabled from the package layout on macOS x64.

## What Changed

- Added an `x86_64-apple-darwin` row to the macOS zsh release matrix.
- Runs that row on `macos-15-large`, the Intel macOS runner appropriate for the native zsh build.
- Added the matching `macos-x86_64` platform to `.github/dotslash-zsh-config.json` so the generated DotSlash release manifest can reference the new tarball.

## Testing

- `ruby -e "require \"yaml\"; YAML.load_file(\".github/workflows/rust-release-zsh.yml\"); puts \"ok\""`
- `python3 -m json.tool .github/dotslash-zsh-config.json`
items.title: release: build macOS x64 zsh artifact

## Summary

- Map Responses API `.image_url` `invalid_value` 400s into `InvalidImageRequest` so existing invalid-image recovery can run for empty/invalid base64 image URL failures.
- Replace empty `data:image/*;base64,` user images with model-visible text instead of emitting an `input_image` item.
- Replace empty base64 image outputs from MCP and dynamic tool paths with text feedback before they are serialized as tool output images.

## Why

Empty base64 image URLs are a known low-level poisoned-thread shape. They are always invalid for the Responses API, and letting them through causes later turns or resumes to replay the same bad `image_url` and fail before the model can recover.

This keeps the scope intentionally narrow: it does not add a broad image validator, durable history patching, or all-image replacement semantics.

## Validation

- `just fmt`
- `cargo test -p codex-api`
- `cargo test -p codex-protocol`
- `git diff --check`

Not run: full workspace test suite.
items.title: [codex] reject empty base64 image inputs

# Why

Prompt hooks let hook authors express review criteria as model-evaluated prompts while preserving Codex hook semantics. Codex should default these checks to the active thread model instead of a fixed hook model.

# What

- Add `type = "prompt"` hook handler config, app-server API, generated schemas, and hook list support with optional `model`, `timeout`, and `continueOnBlock`.
- Wire prompt hooks into the hook engine for PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, and Stop while skipping unsupported events with warnings.
- Add a core prompt-hook runner that calls the model with no tools, defaults to the thread model, and expects `{ "ok": boolean, "reason": string }`.
- Map `ok: false` to Codex event-specific outcomes: deny pre-tool-use, block/continue post-tool-use according to `continueOnBlock`, block user prompt and stop hooks, and no-op permission requests.
- Add a Stop integration test in the style of Claude multi-criteria hooks, requiring the assistant to revise once before the prompt hook returns ok.

Fixes #24249.

## Why

Codex already supports discovering marketplaces under both `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. The Git marketplace auto-upgrade no-op check only looked for the `.agents` layout, though. That meant an installed `.claude-plugin` marketplace with matching revision metadata still looked absent, so plugin list/startup upgrade work could stage and re-activate the same marketplace again. In #24249, that repeated upgrade path lined up with a malformed `source: "./"` plugin entry and produced the observed marketplace sync churn.

## What changed

- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/marketplace_upgrade.rs` now uses the existing supported marketplace manifest discovery helper when deciding whether an installed Git marketplace is already current.
- Existing local plugin source validation is unchanged; `source: "./"` still remains invalid.

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-core-plugins`

items.body: ## Why Empty base64 image URLs are a known poisoned-thread shape. They are always invalid for the Responses API, and letting them through can make later turns or resumes replay the same bad `image_url` and fail before the model can recover. This PR handles the lowest-risk sources of that shape by rejecting empty user image inputs before a turn is submitted, normalizing empty tool image outputs before serialization, and mapping the two relevant backend image sanitizer failures into the existing invalid-image recovery path. The bridge mapping intentionally mirrors the relevant server messages from `openai/api/libs/image-processing-common/image_processing_common/image_service.py`: - `IMAGE_PARSE_ERROR`: `The image data you provided does not represent a valid image` - `IMAGE_INVALID_BASE64`: `Expected a base64-encoded data URL with an image MIME type` ## What Changed - In `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs`, reject empty `data:image/*;base64,` user image inputs before `turn/start` or `turn/steer` submits work to core. This is intentionally small: a predicate, an internal JSON-RPC error helper, and explicit checks at the two submit boundaries. - In `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, stop converting empty user images into model-visible placeholder text. User-image rejection now happens before turn submission. - In `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, replace empty base64 MCP image outputs with tool-output text before they are serialized as image output. - In `codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs`, apply the same empty-base64 guard to dynamic tool image output conversion as a defensive normalization point. - In `codex-rs/codex-api/src/api_bridge.rs`, map backend image parse and invalid-base64 400s into `CodexErr::InvalidImageRequest()` using phrase constants that match the server messages. - Add focused coverage for the bridge mapping, empty MCP images, and app-server rejection before `turn/started`. ## App UX Before: After: ## Related Issues This issue is a primary cause of permanent thread poisoning by invalid images. GitHub issues in the empty-base64 `image_url` family: - [#23558](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/23558) - [#22886](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/22886) Also relevant for the empty-base64 replay variant, though broader than this exact fix: - [#22442](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/22442) Relevant Sentry examples: - [CODEX-Y34](https://openai.sentry.io/issues/CODEX-Y34/) - Numbers spreadsheet-row paste treated as image/PNG with empty base64. - [CODEX-1C7A](https://openai.sentry.io/issues/CODEX-1C7A/) - Windows Desktop empty-base64 `image_url` 400. - [CODEX-13SZ](https://openai.sentry.io/issues/CODEX-13SZ/) - Repeated 400s from empty-base64 `image_url`. - [CODEX-S5P](https://openai.sentry.io/issues/CODEX-S5P/) - Tool-output `input[...].output[1].image_url` empty-base64 rejection. ## Validation - `just fmt` - `just test -p codex-api` - `just test -p codex-protocol` - `just test -p codex-app-server` - `just fix -p codex-protocol` - `just fix -p codex-app-server` - After the final app-server churn reduction: `just test -p codex-app-server turn_start_rejects_empty_base64_image_before_starting_turn` - `git diff --check` Not run: full workspace test suite.

items.body:
# Why

Codex needs a durable way to publish shell environment changes for later local command executions without rewriting the command that users and approval policy see.

Hooks can append shell export lines to a session env file, and subsequent local shell-like commands run with those exports applied. In Codex, the primary interface is `CODEX_ENV_FILE` while `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` is a compatibility alias.

# What

- Add a per-thread `CODEX_ENV_FILE` path and expose the same path as `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` to `SessionStart` hook commands.
- Apply the env file as a local environment overlay for later `shell_command` and local unified exec commands, including `PATH` prepends, without wrapping or rewriting the visible command.
- Support simple export-style persisted updates: `export NAME=value` and Bash `declare -x NAME=value`, with basic `$VAR` and `${VAR}` expansion against the command environment.
- Preserve escaped dollars in double-quoted values, so `export TEMPLATE="\$HOME/bin"` persists the literal `$HOME/bin` instead of expanding it.
- Reset the env file at each real `SessionStart` boundary before hooks run, so resume/clear/compact starts do not accumulate duplicate appends and removed hooks stop affecting later starts.
- Keep the overlay local-only for now; remote unified exec explicitly skips persisted hook env application.
items.title: Add CODEX_ENV_FILE env persistence

items.body:
# Why

A customer reported an MCP server that updates `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` during startup to set shell env. The first session used stale env; the second session worked because config was loaded after the edit existed.

# What

- Force one initial MCP tool discovery before constructing a turn context, then reload user config.
- Refresh `shell_environment_policy` from the refreshed user layer so shell tools see edits without a new session.
- Add an app-server repro with fresh `CODEX_HOME`, a mock MCP server, and a first-turn shell command that reads the MCP-provided env var.

# Bug and RCA

During session creation Codex reads config before optional MCP servers finish starting. For optional servers, startup/tool discovery is asynchronous and can happen after the session is returned to app-server clients. The first turn then builds `TurnContext` from the stale in-memory `Config`, including `permissions.shell_environment_policy`.

The customer MCP server writes `[shell_environment_policy.set]` while handling initial `tools/list`. Before this change, that write was visible on disk by the time tools were used, but the already-created turn context still had the pre-startup shell env policy. A later session worked because config loading started after the TOML edit existed.

There was a second reload gap: `reload_user_config_layer()` refreshed the layer stack and a few derived pieces such as tool suggestions, but it did not rematerialize `shell_environment_policy`. So even an explicit reload could keep the old shell env policy in live session state.

The fix is to do initial MCP discovery once before creating turn contexts, then reload the user layer and rematerialize the shell env policy from the effective config.

# Validation

- `just test -p codex-app-server thread_start_reloads_config_written_by_mcp_startup_before_first_shell_command` passed before the test was renamed to `first_turn_uses_config_written_during_mcp_startup`
- `just test -p codex-core refresh_runtime_config_updates_runtime_refreshable_fields_and_keeps_session_static_settings`
- `just fix -p codex-core`
- `just fix -p codex-app-server`
- `just fmt`
items.title: Fix MCP startup config reload race

items.body:
## Why

Mitigates #24425

A rollout write can fail after partially appending a JSONL record. The retry path then reopens the same file and writes the pending item again, which can splice a partial record and a retried full record onto the same physical line. That leaves the rollout unreadable even though the retried item itself is valid JSON.

## What changed

- Roll back a failed JSONL line write to the file length captured before the write started.
- Repair the final rollout line before appending: preserve valid JSONL that is missing only its trailing newline, and truncate malformed trailing fragments.
- Open rollout files with read/write access so repair and rollback can truncate on platforms where append-only handles are not sufficient.
- Log `ErrorKind` and raw OS errno for rollout writer failures so future filesystem failures are easier to diagnose.
items.title: Harden rollout JSONL writes

## Why
Rejected `turn/start` requests currently disappear from analytics. We already classify rejected `turn/steer` requests, but the reducer ignored `turn/start` error responses entirely, so validation failures such as oversized input had no dedicated event.

## What changed
- add `TurnStartRejectionReason` and a dedicated `codex_turn_start_rejected_event`
- emit rejected `turn/start` events from the analytics reducer with request metadata, image count, and `created_at`
- reuse the existing `AnalyticsJsonRpcError::Input(InputError::TooLarge)` signal to map oversized `turn/start` validation failures to `input_too_large`
- add analytics coverage for serialization, reason mapping, request-metadata propagation, and the no-resurrection case for late responses

## Verification
- `just fmt`
- `just test -p codex-analytics`
- `just test -p codex-app-server turn_start_rejects_combined_oversized_text_input`

items.body:
## Summary
Session-provided model provider config can be owned by a different config authority than the app-server process credentials. If Codex pairs a session-provided `base_url` with process-owned credentials from `auth.json` or environment variables, requests can be sent to one provider with another scope's credentials, as reported in #24457.

This change tightens the boundary in two places:

- Runtime provider auth now ignores the base `AuthManager` unless the selected provider explicitly sets `requires_openai_auth = true`. Provider-owned auth such as `experimental_bearer_token` still takes precedence.
- `SessionThreadConfig` rejects session-scoped provider definitions that would read process-owned credentials through `requires_openai_auth`, `env_key`, or `env_http_headers`.

Fixes #24457
items.title: Keep session providers from process-owned auth

## Why

I realized that we support `AGENTS.override.md` for local repos, but if this file is gitignored (as it often is), we fail to copy it in worktrees and we never look for the copy in the upstream branch. This PR instructs the agent, when in a worktree, to follow the upstream branch in search of a `AGENTS.override.md` file to use.

## What changed

- When discovering project instructions in a linked worktree, check the primary checkout for the corresponding `AGENTS.override.md` when the worktree does not provide one.
- Preserve existing precedence: a worktree-local `AGENTS.override.md` remains first, and an inherited primary-checkout override wins over checked-in `AGENTS.md`.
- Add a regression test for inheriting a primary-checkout override from a linked worktree.

## Verification

- `just fmt`
- `cargo test -p codex-core agents_md --lib`
items.title: core: inherit AGENTS.override.md in linked worktrees

## Why

The memories extension now owns prompt/context contribution and read/retrieval tools, but those tools need a separate rollout switch from the base memories feature. This lets the extension stay installed while hosts opt into exposing the custom tools only when that rollout is intentional.

## What changed

- Added structured `[features.memories]` config with `enabled` and `custom_tools`.
- Preserved the existing boolean `features.memories = true` behavior for enabling the base memories feature.
- Registered the memories extension tool contributor, but only contributes tools when `features.memories.custom_tools` is true.
- Regenerated the config schema so `features.memories` accepts either a boolean or the nested config table.
- Added coverage for TOML parsing, `custom_tools` not enabling memories by itself, extension tool registration, and tool gating.

Example:

```toml
[features.memories]
enabled = true
custom_tools = true
```

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-features`
- `just test -p codex-memories-extension`
- `just test -p codex-config`
- `just test -p codex-core config_schema_matches_fixture`
items.title: Gate memories extension tools behind feature config

items.body:
## Why

`request_user_input` is intended to be modal: once the model asks a question, the current turn must stop until the user answers.

Before this PR there were two problems in Default mode:

1. The tool is only exposed when `features.default_mode_request_user_input = true`, even though asking a clarification question is normal Default-mode behavior.
2. When that flag is enabled together with code mode, `request_user_input` has ordinary direct-tool exposure. This makes it eligible for code-mode nesting. With `code_mode_only` enabled, the modal tool is hidden from the normal model-visible tool list and routed through `exec` instead.

The second behavior violates the tool contract. An `exec` call can continue, complete, or be torn down while the UI is still waiting for a response to the nested question. From a user's perspective, the question appears, but the model does not actually pause; if they do not answer quickly, the pending question appears to expire or time out.

## History

Default-mode question support was originally introduced by Charley Cunningham in #12735, merged on February 25, 2026. That PR allowed `request_user_input` in Default mode, but shipped it behind the `default_mode_request_user_input` opt-in flag.

A later closed, unmerged PR (#13798) explored making the feature default-on before moving it back behind `/experimental`. I did not find a documented product or technical reason for keeping Default-mode questions opt-in.

This PR completes the original Default-mode behavior without the feature flag and fixes the modal-routing issue exposed when `request_user_input` interacts with code mode.

## What Changed

- Make `request_user_input` available in Default and Plan modes without an opt-in feature flag.
- Treat `features.default_mode_request_user_input` as a removed, accepted no-op key so existing configs do not fail.
- Set `request_user_input` to `ToolExposure::DirectModelOnly`, keeping it directly model-visible under `code_mode` and `code_mode_only` while excluding it from the nested `exec` surface.
- Align Default-mode instructions to use the modal tool when it is available, while preserving the plain-text fallback for hosts without it.
- Do not advertise `request_user_input` in `codex exec` or non-root agent tool plans, whose handlers cannot service a modal question.
- Update regression coverage for mode availability, Default-mode round trips, direct modal exposure, unsupported session sources, legacy config handling, and the app-server tool description.

## How to Test

1. Start Codex in normal Default mode without setting `features.default_mode_request_user_input`.
2. Prompt: `Before doing anything, ask me exactly one multiple-choice clarification question about whether to use notes.txt, draft.txt, or todo.txt, then stop and wait for my answer.`
3. Confirm that the question UI appears and the turn remains blocked until an answer is selected.
4. Enable `code_mode` and `code_mode_only`, repeat the prompt, and confirm that `request_user_input` is still a direct modal tool rather than being routed through `exec`.
5. Leave the question unanswered briefly and confirm that it remains pending until the user responds.

Targeted automated tests:

- `just test -p codex-core --retries 0 request_user_input_is_hidden_from_unsupported_session_sources`
- `just test -p codex-core --retries 0 code_mode_only`
- `just test -p codex-models-manager --retries 0 default_mode_instructions_replace_mode_names_placeholder`

All three commands pass; each recipe also completes `just bench-smoke`.

## Validation Notes

- `just fmt` and `just fix -p codex-core -p codex-models-manager` completed for the review follow-up.
- `./tools/argument-comment-lint/run.py -p codex-core -p codex-models-manager` completed successfully for the modified Rust crates.
- Earlier feature validation also completed `just write-config-schema` and scoped `just fix` across the initially affected crates.
items.title: feat(core): enable default-mode user questions
